CALIFORNIA RESIDENTIAL LEASE AGREEMENT

This Residential Lease Agreement ("Agreement") is entered into on March 14, 2026, by and between Harbor Oak Residential LLC, a California limited liability company ("Landlord"), and Priya Raman and Daniel Ortiz, jointly and severally ("Tenant"), for the residential premises located at 1824 Westmoreland Avenue, Apartment 3C, Los Angeles, California 90006 ("Premises"). The Premises is an unfurnished one-bedroom apartment in a twelve-unit building constructed in 1962.

1. TERM. The initial term of this Agreement begins on April 1, 2026, and ends on March 31, 2027 (the "Initial Term"). If Tenant remains in possession after the Initial Term ends with Landlord's consent and no new written agreement has been signed, the tenancy continues as a month-to-month tenancy on the same terms, terminable by either party under Section 23.

2. RENT. Tenant shall pay Landlord monthly rent of $2,450.00, due in advance on the first day of each calendar month, without demand or offset except as permitted by law. Rent may be paid by personal check, cashier's check, money order, electronic transfer, or through Landlord's online tenant portal at no additional charge, and Landlord shall accept at least one form of payment that is neither cash nor electronic funds transfer. Rent for any partial month shall be prorated on a thirty-day basis.

3. LATE CHARGE AND RETURNED PAYMENTS. If rent is not received by the fifth day of the month, Tenant shall pay a one-time late charge of $75.00 for that month, which the parties agree is a reasonable estimate of the administrative costs Landlord incurs from a late payment and not a penalty. If a check or electronic payment is returned unpaid, Tenant shall pay a returned-payment fee of $25.00 for the first occurrence and $35.00 for each subsequent occurrence, as permitted by California Civil Code Section 1719. No other recurring fee or surcharge applies beyond the rent stated in Section 2 unless both parties agree to it in writing.

4. SECURITY DEPOSIT. Tenant shall pay a security deposit of $2,450.00, equal to one month's rent, before taking possession of the Premises. The deposit is not an advance payment of rent and may not be used by Tenant in place of the last month's rent. Landlord may claim from the deposit only the amounts reasonably necessary to cover unpaid rent, to repair damage caused by Tenant beyond ordinary wear and tear, to clean the Premises to the level of cleanliness it was in at the start of the tenancy, and to restore or replace Tenant's personal property where this Agreement so provides. Landlord may not deduct the cost of routine painting, routine carpet cleaning, or repairs that address ordinary wear and tear or conditions that existed before Tenant took possession.

5. RETURN OF SECURITY DEPOSIT. Within twenty-one calendar days after Tenant vacates the Premises, Landlord shall return the security deposit to Tenant, less any lawful deductions, together with an itemized written statement describing each deduction and its amount, and shall attach copies of bills, invoices, or receipts for any deduction over $125.00. Landlord shall take photographs of the Premises within a reasonable time before or at the start of the tenancy, again within a reasonable time after Tenant vacates and before any repair or cleaning work, and again after that work is completed, and shall provide those photographs to Tenant along with the itemized statement.

6. INITIAL INSPECTION. No earlier than two weeks before the tenancy ends, Tenant may request an initial inspection of the Premises and has the right to be present for it. If Tenant requests one, Landlord shall give Tenant a written itemized statement of the repairs and cleaning that Landlord then proposes to deduct from the deposit, so that Tenant has the opportunity to do the work and avoid the deduction before moving out.

7. CONDITION OF PREMISES. Tenant has examined the Premises, including the fixtures and appliances, and agrees that they are in good, clean, and habitable condition except as noted on the move-in condition checklist signed by both parties and attached as Addendum A. Tenant shall return the Premises at the end of the tenancy in the same condition, allowing for ordinary wear and tear.

8. UTILITIES. Tenant is responsible for establishing and paying for electricity and gas serving the Premises in Tenant's own name within five days of taking possession. Landlord is responsible for water, sewer, and trash collection. The Premises is individually metered for electricity and gas, and Landlord does not bill Tenant for any shared or master-metered utility service.

9. LANDLORD'S DUTY TO MAINTAIN. Landlord shall maintain the Premises in a habitable condition as required by California Civil Code Sections 1941 and 1941.1, including effective waterproofing, working plumbing, hot and cold running water, working heating, safe electrical systems, clean and sanitary common areas, adequate trash receptacles, working locks on exterior doors, and floors, stairs, and railings in good repair. Tenant shall notify Landlord in writing, or through the maintenance request function of the tenant portal, as soon as Tenant becomes aware of a condition requiring repair, and Landlord shall begin the repair within a reasonable time after receiving that notice.

10. TENANT'S DUTY TO MAINTAIN. Tenant shall keep the Premises clean and sanitary, dispose of trash properly, use the plumbing, electrical, and heating systems only for their intended purposes, and avoid damaging or defacing the Premises. Tenant is responsible for replacing light bulbs, testing the smoke and carbon monoxide alarms monthly, and replacing alarm batteries during the tenancy, and shall notify Landlord in writing if an alarm is inoperable.

11. ALTERATIONS. Tenant shall not paint, install or remove fixtures, change locks, or make other alterations to the Premises without Landlord's prior written consent, which Landlord shall not unreasonably withhold for minor, reversible alterations. Tenant may install reasonable accessibility modifications as permitted by federal and California fair housing law, subject to Landlord's right to require restoration at the end of the tenancy where restoration is reasonable.

12. RIGHT OF ENTRY. Landlord may enter the Premises only to make necessary or agreed repairs, to supply agreed services, to inspect a waterbed, to show the Premises to prospective tenants, purchasers, lenders, contractors, or inspectors, to conduct the initial inspection described in Section 6, or when otherwise permitted by California Civil Code Section 1954. Except in an emergency, where Tenant has abandoned or surrendered the Premises, or where Tenant and Landlord agree otherwise at the time, Landlord shall give Tenant written notice at least twenty-four hours before entering, or at least six days before entering for the initial inspection, and shall enter only during normal business hours unless Tenant consents to another time.

13. PETS AND ASSISTANCE ANIMALS. Tenant may keep up to two household pets weighing no more than forty pounds each, subject to Landlord's written pet policy attached as Addendum B and to a refundable pet deposit of $300.00, which forms part of the security deposit and counts toward the limit described in Section 4. A service animal or support animal that a person with a disability requires is not a pet, is not subject to the pet deposit or to any pet rent, and Landlord shall treat a request to keep one as a request for reasonable accommodation under fair housing law.

14. OCCUPANCY AND GUESTS. The Premises shall be used only as a private residence for the Tenants named above and for any minor children of Tenant. Tenant may host guests without prior approval, and a guest who stays more than fourteen consecutive days, or more than thirty days in any twelve-month period, shall be discussed with Landlord and may need to be added to this Agreement.

15. SUBLETTING AND ASSIGNMENT. Tenant shall not sublet the Premises, assign this Agreement, or list the Premises on a short-term rental platform without Landlord's prior written consent. Landlord shall not unreasonably withhold consent to a proposed replacement tenant who meets Landlord's written, uniformly applied screening standards.

16. SMOKING. Smoking of any substance, including tobacco, cannabis, and electronic cigarettes, is prohibited inside the Premises, on the balconies and patios, and in all interior common areas of the building. Smoking is permitted only in the designated area at the rear of the parking lot as marked on the site plan in Addendum C, and this section is given as the smoking policy disclosure required by California Civil Code Section 1947.5.

17. INSURANCE. Landlord's insurance does not cover Tenant's personal property or Tenant's liability to others, and Tenant is strongly encouraged to maintain a renter's insurance policy during the tenancy. Tenant is not required to purchase renter's insurance as a condition of this Agreement.

18. RENT INCREASES AND JUST CAUSE NOTICE. California law limits the amount your rent can be increased. See Section 1947.12 of the Civil Code for more information. California law also provides that after all of the tenants have continuously and lawfully occupied the property for 12 months or more or at least one of the tenants has continuously and lawfully occupied the property for 24 months or more, a landlord must provide a statement of cause in any notice to terminate a tenancy. See Section 1946.2 of the Civil Code for more information.

19. NOTICE OF RENT INCREASE. Rent shall not increase during the Initial Term. For any month-to-month tenancy that follows, Landlord shall give Tenant written notice at least thirty days before a rent increase of ten percent or less, and at least ninety days before a rent increase of more than ten percent measured against the lowest rent charged during the preceding twelve months, as required by California Civil Code Section 827.

20. LEAD-BASED PAINT DISCLOSURE. Housing built before 1978 may contain lead-based paint, and lead from paint, paint chips, and dust can pose health hazards if not managed properly, with lead exposure being especially harmful to young children and pregnant women. Landlord has no knowledge of lead-based paint or lead-based paint hazards in the Premises and has no reports or records relating to them, and Landlord has given Tenant the federally approved pamphlet "Protect Your Family From Lead in Your Home," attached as Addendum D.

21. MEGAN'S LAW DISCLOSURE. Notice: Pursuant to Section 290.46 of the Penal Code, information about specified registered sex offenders is made available to the public via an Internet Web site maintained by the Department of Justice at www.meganslaw.ca.gov. Depending on an offender's criminal history, this information will include either the address at which the offender resides or the community of residence and ZIP Code in which he or she resides.

22. ADDITIONAL DISCLOSURES. Landlord discloses that Landlord is not aware of any mold in the Premises that exceeds permissible exposure limits or poses a health threat; that Landlord has given Tenant the state-approved bed bug information notice attached as Addendum E, and that Tenant shall report any suspected bed bug infestation promptly and cooperate with inspection and treatment; that Landlord is not aware that the Premises lies within one mile of a former federal or state military ordnance site; that no demolition permit has been applied for or issued for the building; that to Landlord's knowledge the Premises is not in a special flood hazard area or an area of potential flooding; and that no death occurred in the Premises during the three years before the date of this Agreement.

23. ENDING A MONTH-TO-MONTH TENANCY. If the tenancy becomes month-to-month under Section 1, Tenant may end it by giving Landlord at least thirty days' written notice. Landlord may end it by giving Tenant at least thirty days' written notice if every Tenant has lived in the Premises less than one year, or at least sixty days' written notice if any Tenant has lived there one year or more, and any such notice must satisfy the just cause requirements referenced in Section 18 where those requirements apply.

24. EARLY TERMINATION BY TENANT. If Tenant needs to end this Agreement before the Initial Term expires, Tenant shall give Landlord at least thirty days' written notice and shall remain responsible for rent only until the earlier of the end of that notice period or the date Landlord re-rents the Premises, plus a lease-break fee equal to one month's rent. Landlord shall make reasonable, good-faith efforts to re-rent the Premises promptly in order to limit the rent Tenant owes under this section.

25. STATUTORY TERMINATION RIGHTS. Nothing in this Agreement limits Tenant's right to end the tenancy early where California law allows it, including early termination by a servicemember who receives qualifying orders under Military and Veterans Code Section 400, and early termination by a tenant who is a victim of domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, human trafficking, elder or dependent adult abuse, or another violent crime, upon giving the notice and documentation described in California Civil Code Section 1946.7.

26. DEFAULT AND REMEDIES. If Tenant fails to pay rent when due or otherwise breaches this Agreement, Landlord may serve the notice required by law and, if the breach is not cured within the time that notice allows, may pursue the remedies available under California law, including ending the tenancy and recovering possession through an unlawful detainer action. Landlord shall not attempt to recover possession by locking Tenant out, removing Tenant's belongings, shutting off utilities, or any other means outside the court process.

27. ATTORNEY'S FEES. If either party brings a legal action to enforce this Agreement, the prevailing party may recover reasonable attorney's fees and costs up to a maximum of $1,000.00, and this section applies equally to both parties regardless of which party brought the action.

28. WAIVER OF RIGHTS VOID. Any provision of this Agreement that purports to waive or limit Tenant's rights under California Civil Code Sections 1941 through 1942.5, Tenant's right to notice before entry, Tenant's procedural rights in an unlawful detainer action, or any other right that California law makes non-waivable, is void and unenforceable under California Civil Code Section 1953, and the rest of this Agreement remains in effect.

29. NOTICES. Notices to Landlord shall be delivered to Harbor Oak Residential LLC, 500 South Vermont Avenue, Suite 210, Los Angeles, California 90020, which is also the address at which Landlord receives rent and accepts legal service. Notices to Tenant shall be delivered to Tenant at the Premises, personally, by mail, or by another method permitted under California Code of Civil Procedure Section 1162.

30. JOINT AND SEVERAL LIABILITY. Each person who signs this Agreement as Tenant is individually responsible for the full amount of rent and for every other obligation of Tenant under this Agreement, and notice given to one Tenant counts as notice to all.

31. SEVERABILITY AND GOVERNING LAW. This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of California and by any applicable ordinance of the City of Los Angeles and the County of Los Angeles. If any provision of this Agreement is found unenforceable, the remaining provisions stay in effect.

32. ENTIRE AGREEMENT. This Agreement, together with Addenda A through E, is the entire agreement between the parties about the Premises and replaces all prior negotiations, representations, and agreements, whether written or oral. It may be changed only by a written amendment signed by both parties.

ADDENDA. A: Move-in condition checklist. B: Pet policy. C: Site plan and designated smoking area. D: "Protect Your Family From Lead in Your Home" pamphlet and lead disclosure acknowledgment. E: State-approved bed bug information notice.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have executed this Agreement as of the date first written above.

LANDLORD: Harbor Oak Residential LLC, by Marisol Reyes, Managing Member. Date: ______________

TENANT: Priya Raman. Date: ______________

TENANT: Daniel Ortiz. Date: ______________
